subject: Re: Privacy guarantees, subprocessor routing and evidence path for EU traffic
messages:
From: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@clearhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@clearhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00+00:00
Subject: Initial DPA redline + operational asks (no-training + onshore routing)

Hi David / Kimberly,

Thanks for the time on the call yesterday. Attached is our annotated DPA (ClearHealth_DPA_redline_v2.pdf) — legal flagged two principal operational asks we need to close before procurement: 

1) A contract-level commitment that ClearHealth data will not be used to train or improve any models (no-training / no-derivatives clause). We understand vendors often use operational controls; our counsel wants explicit language + evidence pathway for audits.

2) Subprocessor transparency and residency: we need a current inventory of subprocessors plus attestations that any subprocessors processing EU personal data will either be onshore in the EU or operate under agreements and technical controls (onshore routing or guaranteed onshore KMS).

3) Evidence pack cadence: legal asked whether you can provide an "evidence pack" (attestations, logs summary, subprocessor audit dates) monthly, or alternatively a one-time escrow/third-party verification for the DPA items.

We also attached our SOW (ClearHealth_SOW.docx) to show traffic patterns — most traffic will be EU-resident customer interactions. Can you confirm: a) whether Redwood can commit contractually to a no-training clause, and b) what evidence you can offer and the expected delivery timeline?

Appreciate a short reply with the operational path (we can then loop procurement).

Best,
Emma
Emma Lowe
Head of Privacy & Policy
ClearHealth Systems

Attachments: ClearHealth_DPA_redline_v2.pdf, ClearHealth_SOW.docx

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T11:24:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + operational asks (no-training + onshore routing)

Hi Emma — thanks, and great summary. Short answers up front, followed by operational details and next steps.

High-level commitments we can make:
- Contract clause: Redwood can accept a firm "no-training/no-model-improvement" commitment for the data types defined in the DPA (we'll propose precise wording that matches your redline).
- Operational enforcement: we will enforce the commitment via tenant-level isolation, disabled training flags, and exclusion from our model improvement telemetry pipelines.
- Subprocessors: we will deliver a current subprocessor inventory and signed attestations for any subprocessors that may touch EU personal data. We will mark which subprocessors are onshore and which are covered by additional contractual/technical controls.

Evidence path and timeline:
- Within 5 business days: deliver subprocessor_inventory.csv (contains name, function, region, latest attestation date).
- Within 10 business days: provide a sample evidence pack (S3/Drive) that includes: subprocessor attestations, summary audit log snippet (token-level masking), and a short operational runbook describing how we enforce the no-train toggle.
- Ongoing: monthly evidence packs available on request; for customers requiring continuous oversight we can discuss restricted read-only access to a limited audit bucket.

Onshore routing / KMS options:
- For EU-resident traffic we can configure regional routing to onshore Dedicated capacity (if you purchase reserved capacity) or route through EU-hosted hosted nodes with EU KMS keys. Onshore routing for all traffic requires either a Dedicated commitment or a NetOps-approved routing SLA; we can scope both.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory.csv (stub) — this is a working extract; we'll follow up with full attestations.

Next step: Kimberly and I can propose exact DPA language and a delivery schedule. Can you confirm whether your legal team prefers a monthly evidence cadence or a one-time third-party verification? If they prefer third-party verification, please share acceptable vendors or scope.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-12T08:03:00+00:00
Subject: INTERNAL: ClearHealth follow-up — pricing and ops impact for onshore routing / evidence pack

Marissa / Jonas / Kimberly — looping you in to align on commercialization and implementation. Key asks from ClearHealth: contract-level no-training, monthly evidence pack (or third-party verification), and onshore routing for EU traffic.

Quick proposed plan and asks: 
- Marissa: confirm whether we should price Dedicated onshore routing as a Must-Have (high impact) or offer as optional add-on. Also need guidance if evidence packs are billable as professional services or included at an enterprise tier.
- Jonas: ops feasibility — can we deliver the 5 / 10 business day timeline above for inventory + sample evidence pack? If not, what's realistic and what runbook gaps exist?
- Kimberly: legal to confirm DPA wording draft; also flag any risk with committing to monthly evidence bundles (e.g., sensitive telemetry exposure).

Notes for sales/legal cadence: if ClearHealth takes Dedicated reserved capacity (3–6 month commit), onshore KMS and routing is straightforward. If they remain Hosted, we can still provide EU-hosted tenancy + EU KMS but routing guarantee will be soft (best-effort).

I'll draft the DPA language suggested to match Emma's redline and our operational controls. Target: propose language + inventory within 48 hours.

-David

CONFIDENTIAL: internal coordination only.

From: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@clearhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@clearhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-16T14:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redline + operational asks (no-training + onshore routing)

David / Kimberly — thanks for the clear operational path. Legal reviewed your timeline and is comfortable moving forward on the basis below: 

- We accept Redwood's no-training/no-derivatives commitment pending the exact clause language you share.
- ClearHealth requests monthly evidence packs for the first 6 months (attestations + a sample masked log extract). After 6 months we will revisit cadence.
- For the pilot (90 days) we accept EU-hosted tenancy + EU KMS with the expectation that if traffic exceeds Xqps we'll convert to Dedicated onshore routing. Please bake this conversion path into the SOW.

One final ask: legal prefers third-party verification for critical customers if available. If Redwood can provide an optional escrow/independent attestation (vendor recommendations welcome) we will mark that as preferred.

Please share the proposed DPA redline (DocuSign-ready). I've pasted a DocuSign link below where procurement will expect the redline: 
https://docusign.com/link/CLH-2027-088-DPA-redline

We'll queue procurement upon receipt. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emma
Head of Privacy & Policy
ClearHealth Systems

Attachments referenced: none in this reply (see earlier).
